  • Check the 'To do' at top right first. Overhead ! marks the target of your current task, ? an animal you can care for today, ♥ an animal ready to lead to the ark, and … a family member you haven't talked to today. If the target is off screen, an arrow at the edge points the way.
  • Tools and food are taken out of your bag automatically when you stand in front of what they're for.
  • Eight bird feathers are hidden around the village. Find them all for a small gift (the Journal J shows how many).
  • If your bag is full, sell or put down items to make room.
  • While building the ark, you can gather pitch from the pit up to three times a day; if you run short, buy or trade for it at Hanan's shop.
  • The village grapevines and olive trees bear fruit again three days after you pick them. If you're short on silver, plant crops or trade.
  • When gathering animals, the Journal (J) lists each animal's habitat and favorite food.
  • If you didn't receive the rake, olive leaf or grape cutting inside the ark or on Ararat, make an empty slot and talk to Noah.
  • After sending out the birds, fall asleep in your bed to move on to the next day.

Saving

You can save from the menu ({10}). The game also saves automatically every hour of game time, and when you wake up. It does not save during scenes. On the title screen, 'Continue' opens the save slot you were playing or the most recent one, and 'Load' opens the slot you pick.

Good to know

Play with a keyboard and mouse; on phones and tablets, use the on-screen stick and buttons.
The shortcut bar at the bottom right covers the screen, so it is hidden by default. You can turn it on in Menu → Settings → ‘Shortcut bar’.
A screen of 960×540 or larger is best.
You can scroll the help page or zoom in with your browser.
The help page and the To do can be read by a screen reader.
The game screen must be enjoyed by sight.

Story background

This story starts from Genesis 6–9, the tale of Noah and the great flood. The Bible does not mention a youngest child of Noah. The names of the youngest you play and of the three daughters-in-law (Sedeqa, Nael, Adane), and the family calling Noah's wife 'Mother', are borrowed from tradition and invention. The order of the three brothers, Shem, Ham and Japheth, is also drawn that way for the sake of the story. The flood rain fell for forty days, and life in the ark lasted far longer. In this story the rainy days are shortened to three, and the days of waiting for the waters to recede are skipped with scene changes. The Bible says clean animals came by sevens and the others by pairs. In this story you welcome one representative pair of each kind, and other animals board along with them. On the ark you tend the middle deck. The voice from the sky appears only as golden letters.
